Task: plan a fix for a leftover-hooks regression on branch `fix/uninstall-external-agent-hooks` in /Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/cli/uninstall-ext (git worktree — run everything from there, do not cd to the main checkout). Please plan first; don't start editing until the plan is agreed.

## The bug

Commit `39476dc6` ("Stop reporting a successful uninstall that left hooks behind") changed built-in agents from "always asked to uninstall" to "asked only when the sweep reported hooks installed". But `AreHooksInstalled` asks a narrower question than `UninstallHooks` answers, so a clean "no hooks" is NOT evidence there is nothing to remove:

- claudecode: probes `Stop` alone; removal strips six hook types plus the `permissions.deny` metadata rule, which no probe looks at.
- factoryaidroid: probes 1 hook type, removal strips 7.
- geminicli: probes 10, removal strips 11.
- cursor: the only matched pair.

Repro: `.claude/settings.json` carrying Entire hooks under `SessionStart` + `PreToolUse` plus the deny rule, then `entire disable --uninstall --force`:

```
No agent hooks to remove
Entire CLI uninstalled successfully.   err=<nil>
still contains session-start  : true
still contains pre-tool-use   : true
still contains .entire/metadata : true
```

`.entire/` is deleted, so those surviving hooks now invoke an Entire that is no longer configured there — exactly the end state this branch exists to prevent. Confirmed a regression, not pre-existing: the identical case at `b5f141fe4` (the commit immediately before, on this same branch) returns false for all three.

## Why it's this PR's bug even though the asymmetry is older

I verified the probe/removal gap predates the branch — claudecode's probe was `hasEntireHook(settings.Hooks.Stop)` on `main` too, and the branch changed only its signature (`bool` → `(bool, error)`, to separate "can't tell" from "none"), not what it inspects. `UninstallHooks`'s removal set is unchanged as well.

What the branch changed is how the answer is *used*. On `main`, `removeAgentHooks` calls `UninstallHooks` unconditionally for every agent and uses the probe for one thing only — whether to print a line:

```go
wasInstalled := hs.AreHooksInstalled(ctx)
if err := hs.UninstallHooks(ctx); err != nil { ... } else {
    if wasInstalled { fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Removed %s hooks\n", ag.Type()) }
}
```

So the narrow probe was cosmetic on `main`. `39476dc6` promoted it from a display signal to a gate on whether removal runs at all, and the pre-existing gap became a leftover-hooks bug. The comment that commit deleted named the hazard out loud: *"it still removes hooks a stale AreHooksInstalled fails to recognize."*

## Direction (a patch exists, verified — treat as a starting point, not a mandate)

Skip an agent only when either:
- its check failed (already reported, already fails the command), or
- it is an external plugin that did not report hooks — a subprocess, so don't invoke third-party code speculatively.

Keep asking a built-in that cleanly reported none: the call is in-process and idempotent, so it costs nothing.

That patch was verified: the three artifacts are removed, `go build ./cmd/...` and gofmt clean. The only failing test is `TestRunUninstall_BuiltinNotDetectedIsLeftAlone` (`cmd/entire/cli/setup_test.go:1883`) — it asserts the regressed behaviour and needs inverting, not deleting.

## The open design question — please address it in the plan

The run still prints "No agent hooks to remove" while having actually cleaned a built-in swept blind, because the removal report line is keyed on the sweep's answer rather than on what removal did. That matches pre-regression behaviour but reads wrong, and reporting it accurately needs `UninstallHooks` to say whether it changed anything.

The underlying point: the probe is currently load-bearing for both the gate *and* the report, and it was built for neither. Removal already knows the truth; it just doesn't say it. Worth weighing whether the right fix is `UninstallHooks` returning a "changed anything" signal (and what that costs across all agents, including the external-plugin protocol) versus keeping the report imprecise for now with the gate fixed. Say which you'd pick and why.

Relevant code: `uninstallAgentHooks` and `getAgentHookState` in `cmd/entire/cli/setup.go`, plus each agent's `cmd/entire/cli/agent/*/hooks.go`.

Repo conventions worth honouring: KISS/DRY/TDD (failing test first), tests assert the final positive spec — no narrating the journey or restating history in comments, and `mise run fmt && mise run lint` as a single sequence before anything is considered done.
</cross-session-message>

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)
- dev: TDD Developer agent - implements features using test-driven development and clean code principles (Tools: All tools)

- entire-engineering:design:design-implementation-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to verify that a UI implementation matches its Figma design specifications. This agent should be called after code has been written to implement a design, particularly after HTML/CSS/React components have been created or modified. The agent will visually compare the live implementation against the Figma design and provide detailed feedback on discrepancies.

Examples:
- <example>
  Context: The user has just implemented a new component based on a Figma design.
  user: "I've finished implementing the hero section based on the Figma design"
  assistant: "I'll review how well your implementation matches the Figma design."
  <commentary>
  Since UI implementation has been completed, use the design-implementation-reviewer agent to compare the live version with Figma.
  </commentary>
  </example>
- <example>
  Context: After the general code agent has implemented design changes.
  user: "Update the button styles to match the new design system"
  assistant: "I've updated the button styles. Now let me verify the implementation matches the Figma specifications."
  <commentary>
  After implementing design changes, proactively use the design-implementation-reviewer to ensure accuracy.
  </commentary>
  </example> (Tools: All tools)

- entire-engineering:design:design-iterator: Use this agent PROACTIVELY when design work isn't coming together on the first attempt. If you've made 1-2 design changes and the result still feels off, suggest using this agent with 5x or 10x iterations for deeper refinement. This agent takes screenshots, analyzes what's not working, implements improvements, and repeats N times to systematically fix design issues. Perfect when colors feel wrong, layouts aren't balanced, or the overall aesthetic needs work that single changes can't achieve. <example>Context: User asks to change button color but result still looks off. user: "Change the button to blue" assistant: [makes change, takes screenshot] "The button is now blue, but I notice the overall color balance still feels off. Would you like me to use the design-iterator agent with 5 iterations to systematically improve the color harmony and visual balance?" <commentary>PROACTIVE USE: After a simple change doesn't fully resolve the design issue, suggest the design-iterator to do deeper work.</commentary></example> <example>Context: User's design request leads to something that doesn't look right. user: "Make the hero section more modern" assistant: [makes initial changes] "I've added some modern elements, but the result isn't quite coming together. This looks like it needs iterative refinement. Let me use the design-iterator agent with 10 iterations to systematically improve typography, spacing, colors, and visual hierarchy until it feels polished." <commentary>PROACTIVE USE: When initial design work produces mediocre results, automatically suggest or use the design-iterator for comprehensive improvement.</commentary></example> <example>Context: User wants explicit iterative refinement. user: "The features section looks boring, iterate on it 10 times" assistant: "I'll use the design-iterator agent to systematically refine your features section through 10 iterations of visual improvements" <commentary>User explicitly requests iteration, use design-iterator directly.</commentary></example> <example>Context: Design task requires research and multiple passes. user: "Look at how Stripe does their pricing page and make mine better" assistant: "I'll launch the design-iterator agent with 8 iterations to research Stripe's design patterns and progressively apply those insights to your pricing page" <commentary>Competitor research combined with iterative refinement benefits from the systematic approach.</commentary></example> (Tools: All tools)

Let me review the implementation for simplicity and minimalism using the code-simplicity-reviewer agent" <commentary>Since implementation is complete, use the code-simplicity-reviewer agent to identify simplification opportunities.</commentary></example> <example>Context: The user has written complex business logic and wants to simplify it. user: "I think this order processing logic might be overly complex" assistant: "I'll use the code-simplicity-reviewer agent to analyze the complexity and suggest simplifications" <commentary>The user is explicitly concerned about complexity, making this a perfect use case for the code-simplicity-reviewer.</commentary></example> (Tools: All tools)

- entire-engineering:review:data-integrity-guardian: Use this agent when you need to review database migrations, data models, or any code that manipulates persistent data. - entire-engineering:review:data-migration-expert: Use this agent when reviewing PRs that touch database migrations, data backfills, or any code that transforms production data. This agent validates ID mappings against production reality, checks for swapped values, verifies rollback safety, and ensures data integrity during schema changes. Essential for any migration that involves ID mappings, column renames, or data transformations. <example>Context: The user has a PR with database migrations that involve ID mappings. user: "Review this PR that migrates from action_id to action_module_name" assistant: "I'll use the data-migration-expert agent to validate the ID mappings and migration safety" <commentary>Since the PR involves ID mappings and data migration, use the data-migration-expert to verify the mappings match production and check for swapped values.</commentary></example> <example>Context: The user has a migration that transforms enum values. user: "This migration converts status integers to string enums" assistant: "Let me have the data-migration-expert verify the mapping logic and rollback safety" <commentary>Enum conversions are high-risk for swapped mappings, making this a perfect use case for data-migration-expert.</commentary></example> (Tools: All tools)

- entire-engineering:review:deployment-verification-agent: Use this agent when a PR touches production data, migrations, or any behavior that could silently discard or duplicate records. attachment.content:
- diagnose: Disciplined diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Reproduce → minimise → hypothesise → instrument → fix → regression-test. Use when user says "diagnose this" / "debug this", reports a bug, says something is broken/throwing/failing, or describes a performance regression.
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- github-triage: Triage GitHub issues through a label-based state machine. Use when user wants to create an issue, triage issues, review incoming bugs or feature requests, prepare issues for an AFK agent, or manage issue workflow.
- review-pr-feedback: Walk every unresolved review thread on the current branch's PR — fix what is fixable, ask the user about anything ambiguous, then reply on each thread and mark it resolved. Use when the user says "review PR feedback", "go thru the PR comments", "address review comments", or similar.
- ship: Commit, push, and update the PR description or add a comment based on new changes. Use when the user says "ship it", "commit push and update pr", or similar.
- to-issues: Break a plan, spec, or PRD into independently-grabbable GitHub issues using tracer-bullet vertical slices. Use when user wants to convert a plan into issues, create implementation tickets, or break down work into issues.
- to-prd: Turn the current conversation context into a PRD and submit it as a GitHub issue. Use when user wants to create a PRD from the current context.
- unslop: Cut AI tells from any writing. Must always apply.
- write-a-skill: Create new agent skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and bundled resources. Use when user wants to create, write, or build a new skill.
- agent-integration: Run all three agent integration phases sequentially: research, write-tests, and implement using E2E-first TDD (unit tests written last). For individual phases, use /agent-integration:research, /agent-integration:write-tests, or /agent-integration:implement. Use when the user says "integrate agent", "add agent support", or wants to run the full agent integration pipeline end-to-end.
- changelog: Generate or update the CHANGELOG.md for a new release version. Use when the user says "generate changelog", "update changelog", "write release notes", or asks to prepare a changelog for a version like "changelog for 0.5.3".
- e2e: Orchestrate E2E test triage and fix implementation: runs triage-ci then implement sequentially. Accepts test names, --agent, artifact path, or CI run reference. For individual phases, use /e2e:triage-ci, /e2e:debug, or /e2e:implement. Use when the user says "triage e2e", "fix e2e failures", or wants the full triage-to-fix pipeline.
- test-repo: Use this skill to test strategy changes against a fresh test repository. Invoke when the user asks to "test against a test repo", "validate the changes", or wants to verify session hooks, commits, and rewind functionality work correctly.

## 5. Test conventions in setup_test.go

- **Not table-driven for the uninstall paths.** One test per behaviour, each with a doc comment stating the invariant it pins ("pins that…", "must not…"). Tables appear only for pure functions: `TestEnableUsesSetupFlow` (:2394), `TestCleanRemoteURLForReport` (:4558), `TestShellCompletionTarget` (:2125) — those use `for _, tt := range …` + `t.Run` + nested `t.Parallel()`.
- **`t.Parallel()` is the exception, and its absence is always annotated.** Every non-parallel test carries a one-line reason as the first statement comment, e.g. `// Cannot use t.Parallel: mutates $PATH, cwd, and the agent registry.` Only pure-function tests call `t.Parallel()` (:1744, :2302, :2325, :2395, :4169, :4181, :4455, :4559, :4712).
- **Temp repo via `setupTestRepo`/`setupTestDir`**, relying on `t.TempDir()` + `t.Chdir()` + `t.Setenv()` for automatic cleanup; global agent registry restored with `t.Cleanup(agent.SnapshotRegistryForTesting())`; path caches explicitly cleared.
- **Output asserted as strings, not structs.** Tests pass `var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer` into `runUninstall(ctx, &stdout, &stderr, true)` and use `strings.Contains` on phrase fragments ("did not complete", "has been removed from this repository", "could not check whether", "may or may not remain"). Stream discipline is part of the contract: warnings must be on stderr, verdicts on stdout.
- **Error type is asserted, not just non-nil**: `var silent *SilentError; errors.As(err, &silent)`.
- Failure messages include the captured output (`, stdout:\n%s`) so a failure is diagnosable without a rerun; `t.Fatalf` for preconditions, `t.Errorf` for independent assertions.
- Externally observable side effects are asserted through an exec log file (`ENTIRE_TEST_EXEC_LOG`) with exact counts, e.g. `strings.Count(string(data), "are-hooks-installed") != 1` at setup_test.go:1313.</result>

New single definition, for every built-in agent:

  AreHooksInstalled == "removal would change this config" == at least one Entire-owned artifact is present.

Mechanism (DRY, one code path per agent):
1. Each built-in agent extracts its removal into a PURE function over the config file's bytes:
   `func removeEntireArtifacts(data []byte) (out []byte, changed bool, err error)`
   — `changed` is set by the agent when it actually drops an Entire hook entry / the deny rule / any owned artifact. It is NOT computed by byte-comparing re-marshalled output (that would false-positive on reformatting).
2. New shared helper in package `cmd/entire/cli/agent` (e.g. hook_file.go), used by the JSON-file agents (claudecode, cursor, geminicli, factoryaidroid, copilotcli, codex). 3. codex's `core` distinction is deliberately dropped from `AreHooksInstalled` (freshness stays the job of `MissingEntireHooks` in codex/trust.go and of `CheckHookConfig`/HookFreshness generally).

Be exhaustive — I need a checklist.

B) **Every production behaviour that changes because detection widens.** Trace each consumer of the sweep and say concretely what a user sees differently: `getAgentHookState`/`GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled`/`InstalledAgentDisplayNames`/`OutdatedHookAgents` in cmd/entire/cli/config.go; `entire status`; `entire enable` (including the deselect path at setup.go:636 and `uninstallDeselectedAgentHooks` at setup.go:1637); `entire agent remove` (setup.go:1596); `entire doctor` (doctor.go:601 checkHookDrift, :650 checkCodexHookTrust); the review/investigate pickers; `codex.DetectPresence` (codex/codex.go:56) and `copilotcli.DetectPresence` (copilotcli.go:54). Flag any place that would now MIS-behave (e.g. anything that assumes AreHooksInstalled means "fully and currently installed", or any enable path that skips installing when it returns true).

C) **Hazards in the mechanism itself.** In particular: does any of these agents' UninstallHooks currently have a side effect beyond removing artifacts that would be lost by "write only when changed" (e.g. geminicli's `stripNonArrayHookFields`, which normalises the config; cursor/copilotcli's top-level `version: 1`; claudecode's pruning of empty `hooks`/`permissions`/`deny` containers)? D) The three install/uninstall asymmetries already known (geminicli leaves `hooksConfig.enabled: true`; cursor + copilotcli leave `version: 1`; pi's uninstall does `os.RemoveAll` of the whole extension dir while its install refuses foreign files) — for each, one line on whether it becomes a *correctness* problem under the new definition, or stays cosmetic and out of scope.

Answer as a concrete checklist with file:line. Do not write a plan file.

# B) Production behaviour that changes

Which agents actually widen: **claudecode** (`Stop` → 6 hook types + `permissions.deny`), **factoryaidroid** (`Stop` → 7 types + deny), **codex** (AND of 4 core → OR of 7 events). **cursor** (`cursor/hooks.go:303-311`), **geminicli** (`geminicli/hooks.go:435-441`) and **copilotcli** (`copilotcli/hooks.go:262-269`) already OR over exactly the set their uninstall touches, so for them only the *code path* changes, not the answer — with the two exceptions in C1 and C4.

**B1. `getAgentHookState` — `cmd/entire/cli/config.go:141-172`**
More agents land in `state.installed`. Also: the `default:` branch at `:161-169` (→ `unchecked`) fires on a **different** set of malformed files now. Today the detect path unmarshals the whole file into a typed struct (`loadClaudeSettings` → `ClaudeSettings`, `CursorHooksFile`, `GeminiSettings`, `FactorySettings`, `CopilotHooksFile`), so a garbage value in *any* field errors. The removal path is raw-map and tolerant: `claudecode/hooks.go:341-346` and `factoryaidroid/hooks.go:335-340` explicitly swallow a `permissions` parse failure (`rawPermissions = nil`). Consequence: a repo with `"permissions": "oops"` and a live deny rule moves from **"could not check → uninstall exits non-zero and warns"** to **"cleanly reported, nothing to remove"** — the deny rule silently survives an uninstall that reports success. That is the exact failure mode this branch was written to prevent. The pure function must return an error (not swallow) when it cannot parse a container it is supposed to strip.

**B2. `GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled` / `InstalledAgentDisplayNames` — `config.go:180-187`**
Straight pass-through; every consumer below inherits the widening.

**B3. `entire status` — `status.go:193` (text), `status.go:808` (JSON)**
A user sees `Agents · Codex` (or Claude Code, or Droid) listed where a partial/leftover config previously showed nothing. Concretely: someone who ran `entire enable` on an old release that only wrote Codex `Stop`, or someone whose `.claude/settings.json` has only the `Read(./.entire/metadata/**)` deny rule left behind by a half-finished uninstall, now sees the agent listed as enabled. Defensible — it is what "there is something of ours here" means — but it is a visible change and the deny-rule-only case is the one that reads as a lie.

**B4. `entire agent list` — `agent_group.go:69-88`**
Same widening; the `✓` marker appears against more agents, and the `"No agents installed"` hint at `:84` stops firing in leftover-artifact repos.

**B5. `OutdatedHookAgents` / `OutdatedHookAgentDisplayNames` — `config.go:201-219`; consumed by `status.go:812` and `doctor.go:601-624` (`checkHookDrift`)**
Scoped to `GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled`, so the *candidate* set grows. Only `claudecode` (`claudecode/hooks.go:470`), `pi` (`pi/hooks.go:157`) and `opencode` (`opencode/hooks.go:136`) implement `HookFreshness`, so codex/factory/cursor/gemini/copilot widening has no drift effect. See B7 for what happens to claudecode.

**B6. `entire doctor` — `doctor.go:601` `checkHookDrift`, `doctor.go:642` `checkCodexHookTrust`**
`checkCodexHookTrust` is gated on `os.Stat(.codex/hooks.json)` (`doctor.go:643-647`), **not** on `AreHooksInstalled` — unaffected, and `MissingEntireHooks`/`HookTrustGaps` in `codex/trust.go` are unchanged. `checkHookDrift` is affected via B7.

**B7. MIS-BEHAVIOUR: `checkHookDrift` goes silent on exactly the configs the widening newly reports as installed.**
`claudecode.CheckHookConfig` (`claudecode/hooks.go:476-490`) returns `HooksAbsent` when `!hasEntireHook(settings.Hooks.Stop)`. So a `.claude/settings.json` carrying only `PostToolUse` hooks, or only the deny rule, now:
- `entire status` → `Agents · Claude Code` (B3)
- `entire doctor` → prints **neither** `✓ Claude Code hook config: OK` **nor** `Claude Code hooks: OUT OF DATE`, because `checkHookDrift` treats `HooksAbsent` as "nothing to report" (`doctor.go:611-613`)
- `status --json` → agent listed, `hooks_outdated` empty

i.e. the user is told the agent is enabled and told nothing is wrong, while its `Stop` hook — the one that drives checkpointing — is missing. **Fix required in this change:** `claudecode.CheckHookConfig` must return `HooksOutdated` (not `HooksAbsent`) when detection says installed but the current spec is not met. The cleanest form is to stop using `hasEntireHook(Stop)` as the absent-gate and instead gate on the same "any owned artifact" predicate the new `AreHooksInstalled` uses, then let the positive-spec checks at `:483-487` decide current-vs-outdated. `factoryaidroid` has no `CheckHookConfig` at all, so its widened-detect configs get no drift report either — worth a line in the design even if you leave it.

**B8. `entire agent remove <name>` — `setup.go:1596-1613`**
This is the fix landing. Today `entire agent remove codex` on a Stop-only config prints `Codex hooks are not installed.` (`:1604`) and removes nothing. After: it removes them and prints `Removed Codex hooks.` Same for claudecode/factory with only the deny rule or only tool-use hooks. The error path at `:1597-1602` (fail rather than uninstall blind) is unchanged.

**B9. `entire disable --uninstall` — `setup.go:2419` sweep → `setup.go:2705` `uninstallAgentHooks`**
Agents previously invisible to the sweep are now in `hookState.installed`, so their `UninstallHooks` runs and they appear in the confirmation summary (`setup.go:2440-2452`) and the removal report. Also, the "nothing to uninstall" guard at `setup.go:2427-2433` now falls through in repos whose only trace is a leftover artifact — so `entire disable --uninstall` in such a repo stops saying `Entire is not installed in this repository.` and instead prompts. That is the intended fix, but it is a new prompt in a case that used to be a clean no-op.

**B10. `entire enable` deselect path — `setup.go:1245` → `uninstallDeselectedAgentHooks` (`setup.go:1637-1668`)**
`installedNames` widens, so deselecting an agent with a partial config now actually removes it. Intended fix.

**B11. MIS-BEHAVIOUR: `applyAgentChanges` skips install for anything the sweep calls installed — `setup.go:552-583`, especially `:576-581`.**
`for _, name := range selectedAgentNames { if _, wasInstalled := installedSet[name]; wasInstalled { if opts.ForceHooks { reinstall } ; continue } }`. The `continue` at `:580` means a *selected* agent that the sweep reports installed gets **no** `InstallHooks` call without `--force`. Today a codex config with only `Stop` reports **not** installed → codex lands in `addedAgents` → `setupAgentHooks` runs → `InstallHooks` syncs in the missing 6 events. After the change it reports installed → skipped → **the partial install is never repaired**. Reached by `entire agent` (bare) → `runAgentMenu` (`agent_group.go:52`) → `runManageAgents` (`setup.go:456`) → `applyAgentChanges`.

Not reached by: `entire enable` (`runEnableInteractive`, `setup.go:1249-1252`, calls `setupAgentHooks` for every selected agent unconditionally) or `entire agent add <name>` (`agent_group.go:118` → `setupAgentHooksNonInteractive` → `setupAgentHooks`). So the regression is scoped to the `entire agent` menu, but it is real and it is the "any enable path that skips installing when it returns true" you asked about. `InstallHooks` is idempotent for all six agents (`count==0` early return, e.g. `copilotcli/hooks.go:129`, `cursor/hooks.go:156`, `codex/hooks.go:117`), so the fix is cheap: drop the `continue` and always call `setupAgentHooks` for selected agents, using the returned count to decide whether to print "Added" vs nothing.

**B12. `codex.DetectPresence` — `codex/codex.go:55-57`, feeding `agent.DetectAll` (`agent/registry.go:86`) → `detectOrSelectAgent` (`setup.go:1734`)**
Codex now auto-detects on a partial config. Consequences: on a no-TTY first run, `detected` now includes codex so `entire enable` enables it (`setup.go:1740-1760` + the non-interactive branch); on a TTY it is pre-selected in the multi-select; the `Detected agent: X` / `Detected multiple agents: …` messages (`setup.go:1745`, `:1756`) change wording in repos with a leftover `.codex/hooks.json`. Note the `hasInstalledHooks` branch at `:1735-1738` also flips, so such a repo takes the "re-run" path (no `Detected agent:` line) rather than the first-run path.

**B13. `copilotcli.DetectPresence` — `copilotcli/copilotcli.go:53-55`**
No change: its `AreHooksInstalled` already ORs over exactly the 8 keys uninstall touches. The only way this moves is if you count `version: 1` as owned (C4) — which would make a leftover `{"version":1}` file auto-detect Copilot in every repo that ever had it. Don't.

**B14. Review / investigate pickers**
- `review/cmd.go:370` (`runReviewConfigure`), `:425` (`runReviewListModels` → `availableReviewAgents`), `:534` (`runReviewListAgents`, prints hook-install status), `:816` (`runReview`)
- `investigate/cmd.go:445`, `:617` (`RunInvestigateConfigPicker`), `:833` (`verifyAgentsLaunchable`)
- wired at `review_bridge.go:40` and `investigate_bridge.go:23`

`verifyAgentsLaunchable` (`investigate/cmd.go:833-845`) hard-errors `agent %q is not launchable (run 'entire configure --agent %s' first)` for anything not in the installed set. After the widening, `entire investigate --agent codex` succeeds on a Stop-only config and spawns a reviewer whose `SessionStart` hook never fires — a silently degraded run replacing a clear error. Same shape for `entire review --agent codex`. This is the one consumer where "installed" genuinely meant "fully wired", and it is the strongest argument for landing B7's freshness fix alongside (or for having the pickers consult `HookFreshness` rather than `AreHooksInstalled`).

**B15. `root.go:83` — telemetry `agentStr`**
`GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled` feeds `telemetry.TrackCommandDetached`. Per-command agent attribution now includes leftover/partial agents; any dashboard counting "repos with codex enabled" steps up discontinuously at this release. Cosmetic but worth knowing before someone reads it as adoption.

**B16. `setup.go:1398` `printEnabledStatus`** — post-enable `Agents: …` line widens, same as B3.

# C) Hazards in the mechanism

## C1. geminicli `stripNonArrayHookFields` — the real one
`geminicli/hooks.go:238-249`, called from uninstall at `:338` (return value **discarded**) and from install at `:92` as `cleanupDone`, where it is used to force a write.

It deletes any non-array value under `hooks`, i.e. the legacy `hooks.enabled: true` that old Entire versions wrote. Two facts make this the decision point:
- Gemini CLI 0.33+ **rejects** a `hooks` object with a non-array property (per the comment at `hooks.go:89-91`). So this is not cosmetic normalisation — a config left with `hooks.enabled` is a config Gemini refuses to load.
- `hooks.enabled` is unambiguously an Entire-written artifact. Nobody else put it there.

**Does conditional-on-`changed` lose something?** Yes, in exactly one case: a config with `hooks.enabled: true` and no Entire hook entries (a repo already half-cleaned). Today `UninstallHooks` strips it and writes; under a naive `changed` it would not.
**Should it count as `changed`?** Yes — and the plumbing already exists: `stripNonArrayHookFields` returns a bool, install already treats it as write-forcing, and uninstall already discards it at `:338`. OR it into `changed`. Cost, which you should accept deliberately: `AreHooksInstalled` then returns **true** for a config whose only trace is `hooks.enabled: true`, so `entire status` lists Gemini for such a repo. That is consistent with the new definition ("removal would change this config") and it is arguably right — the file is broken *by us* and we can fix it. The alternative (don't count it) leaves a config Gemini rejects on disk after a "successful" uninstall, which is worse.
**Test consequence:** `geminicli/hooks_test.go:676` keeps passing either way (its fixture has an Entire hook too). Add the no-hook-only-`enabled` case to pin the decision.

## C2. claudecode / factoryaidroid empty-container pruning
`claudecode/hooks.go:363-393` — deletes `permissions.deny` when the filtered list is empty (`:367`), deletes `permissions` when the map is empty (`:379`), deletes `hooks` when `rawHooks` is empty (`:391`). `factoryaidroid/hooks.go:357-387` is the same code.

Today, uninstalling in a repo whose `.claude/settings.json` is `{"hooks": {}, "permissions": {"deny": []}}` (no Entire artifact anywhere) rewrites it to `{}`. Under `changed`-gated writes it is left alone.
**Loses something?** Nothing a user can perceive. Empty `hooks: {}` and `deny: []` are valid, inert, and were most likely written by the user or by another tool, not by us. Claude Code does not reject them.
**Should it count as `changed`?** **No.** Counting it would make `AreHooksInstalled` return true for `{"hooks":{}}` — i.e. `entire status` would list Claude Code in any repo with an empty hooks stanza, and `entire disable --uninstall` would stop reporting "not installed" there. That is a much worse false positive than the cosmetic loss. Set `changed` only from: an Entire hook entry dropped from one of the 6/7 managed types, or the `metadataDenyRule` dropped from `permissions.deny`. Then keep the pruning as an *effect* of the write rather than a trigger for it.
**Watch out for:** the prune currently also runs when `changed` *is* true, which is what makes `TestUninstallHooks_RemovesDenyRule` (`claudecode:374`, `factoryaidroid:547`) read a permissions object that no longer exists via `readPermissions`. Keep the prune inside the pure function's write branch, not outside it.

## C3. claudecode / factoryaidroid swallowed `permissions` parse error
`claudecode/hooks.go:341-346`, `factoryaidroid/hooks.go:335-340`: `if err := json.Unmarshal(permRaw, &rawPermissions); err != nil { rawPermissions = nil }` and the cleanup is skipped silently.

Today this is a hidden uninstall bug (the deny rule survives, uninstall reports success). Under the new design it becomes an **advertised lie**: `AreHooksInstalled` would return `false` for a config that still has the deny rule under an unparseable `permissions`, and `getAgentHookState` would classify it as "cleanly reported no hooks" instead of `unchecked` — losing the warning path at `setup.go:2760-2763`. Fix in this change: return an error from the pure function rather than nil-ing `rawPermissions`. See B1.

## C4. cursor / copilotcli top-level `version: 1`
Written on install (`cursor/hooks.go:76-82`, `copilotcli/hooks.go:63-69`), never removed on uninstall.
**Loses something?** No. Today uninstall re-marshals and rewrites the file even when it changes nothing, so a `{"version":1}`-only file gets a pointless write. Skipping it is strictly better.
**Should it count as `changed`?** **No, emphatically.** Counting it would (a) break `cursor/hooks_test.go:235`, `cursor:499`, `copilotcli:157`, `copilotcli:393` — every "false after uninstall" assertion, since `version` survives — and (b) make a leftover `{"version":1}` file mean "Cursor is installed" forever, including in `copilotcli.DetectPresence` (B13). Keep `version` unowned.

## C5. codex's early return on a missing `hooks` key
`codex/hooks.go:186-188`: `if rawHooks == nil { return nil }` — no write. Already equivalent to `changed=false`; map it straight across. Note codex is the only one of the six with this early-out, so it is the existing precedent for the design.

## C6. Repo-root fallback divergence (small but real)
The six agents currently disagree on the `paths.WorktreeRoot` failure fallback: install uses `os.Getwd()` in claudecode (`hooks.go:69`), geminicli (`hooks.go:48`), codex (`hooks.go:70`); uninstall/detect uses `"."` everywhere (`claudecode/hooks.go:284`, `geminicli/hooks.go:308`, `codex/hooks.go:165`, `cursor/hooks.go:200`, `copilotcli/hooks.go:173`, `factoryaidroid/hooks.go:277`). Functionally identical (both resolve relative to the process cwd), so unifying on `"."` in the shared helper is safe and avoids the `//nolint:forbidigo` that `os.Getwd` needs in this codebase. Just don't unify on `os.Getwd()`.

## C7. The two entry points must not diverge on *ordering*
`AreHooksInstalled` and `UninstallHooks` sharing `removeEntireArtifacts` means detection now pays the full parse+transform cost of a removal, per agent, on every sweep. `getAgentHookState` runs on **every command** via `root.go:83` (telemetry) and on every `status`/`review`/`investigate`/`enable`. There is a benchmark guarding the enable hot path (`bench_enable_test.go`) but not the sweep. Six raw-map round-trips per invocation is still microseconds — worth a note, not a redesign, but do not let the helper also *write* from the detect entry point (the "reports `changed`" entry must be provably read-only, same bar `HookFreshness` sets at `agent/agent.go:161-163`).

## C8. `pi` violates the new invariant and is exempted
`pi/hooks.go:108-118` does `os.RemoveAll(filepath.Dir(path))`. So "removal would change this config" is true whenever the extension **directory** exists, including when it holds only a foreign `index.ts`; but `AreHooksInstalled` (`pi/hooks.go:128-143`) keys on `entireMarker` in the file. Leaving pi alone is the right call — widening it would make the sweep call an `os.RemoveAll` over a directory Entire does not own — but it means the new definition is a convention, not an invariant, and the doc comment on `agent.HookSupport` should say so rather than assert it universally. See D3.

# D) The three known asymmetries under the new definition

**D1. geminicli leaves `hooksConfig.enabled: true` (`geminicli/hooks.go:96`, written by install; absent from uninstall at `:304-402`).**
**Stays cosmetic and out of scope** — and must be *kept* out of scope: it is a top-level Gemini setting, not under `hooks`, and Gemini tolerates it with no hooks present. Counting it as owned would pin `AreHooksInstalled` to `true` forever after uninstall, breaking `geminicli/hooks_test.go:387` and permanently listing Gemini in `entire status`. Distinct from `hooks.enabled` (C1), which is inside `hooks`, breaks Gemini's schema, and *is* removed by uninstall — that one becomes a correctness question and my recommendation is to count it.

**D2. cursor + copilotcli leave `version: 1` (`cursor/hooks.go:76-82`, `copilotcli/hooks.go:63-69`).**
**Stays cosmetic and out of scope.** Must not count as `changed` (C4). The only new visible effect is a *good* one: uninstall stops rewriting a file it does not change.

**D3. pi's uninstall `os.RemoveAll`s the extension dir while install refuses foreign files (`pi/hooks.go:108-118` vs the marker check at `:128-143`).**
**Becomes a stated exception rather than a correctness problem** — because pi is excluded, `AreHooksInstalled` stays marker-gated, and every path that can trigger removal (`setup.go:1596` `entire agent remove`, `setup.go:636`/`1661` deselect, `setup.go:2734` uninstall sweep) is gated on that same marker check, so a foreign-only directory is never reached. It does, however, make pi the counterexample to the invariant the design is trying to establish, so the contract comment at `agent/agent.go:124-133` should be written as "for the JSON-config built-ins" rather than "for every agent", and the `os.RemoveAll` blast radius deserves its own follow-up (narrow it to the marker-carrying file plus a directory removal only when the directory is then empty).

# B) Production behaviour that changes

Which agents actually widen: **claudecode** (`Stop` → 6 hook types + `permissions.deny`), **factoryaidroid** (`Stop` → 7 types + deny), **codex** (AND of 4 core → OR of 7 events). **cursor** (`cursor/hooks.go:303-311`), **geminicli** (`geminicli/hooks.go:435-441`) and **copilotcli** (`copilotcli/hooks.go:262-269`) already OR over exactly the set their uninstall touches, so for them only the *code path* changes, not the answer — with the two exceptions in C1 and C4.

**B1. `getAgentHookState` — `cmd/entire/cli/config.go:141-172`**
More agents land in `state.installed`. Also: the `default:` branch at `:161-169` (→ `unchecked`) fires on a **different** set of malformed files now. Today the detect path unmarshals the whole file into a typed struct (`loadClaudeSettings` → `ClaudeSettings`, `CursorHooksFile`, `GeminiSettings`, `FactorySettings`, `CopilotHooksFile`), so a garbage value in *any* field errors. The removal path is raw-map and tolerant: `claudecode/hooks.go:341-346` and `factoryaidroid/hooks.go:335-340` explicitly swallow a `permissions` parse failure (`rawPermissions = nil`). Consequence: a repo with `"permissions": "oops"` and a live deny rule moves from **"could not check → uninstall exits non-zero and warns"** to **"cleanly reported, nothing to remove"** — the deny rule silently survives an uninstall that reports success. That is the exact failure mode this branch was written to prevent. The pure function must return an error (not swallow) when it cannot parse a container it is supposed to strip.

**B2. `GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled` / `InstalledAgentDisplayNames` — `config.go:180-187`**
Straight pass-through; every consumer below inherits the widening.

**B3. `entire status` — `status.go:193` (text), `status.go:808` (JSON)**
A user sees `Agents · Codex` (or Claude Code, or Droid) listed where a partial/leftover config previously showed nothing. Concretely: someone who ran `entire enable` on an old release that only wrote Codex `Stop`, or someone whose `.claude/settings.json` has only the `Read(./.entire/metadata/**)` deny rule left behind by a half-finished uninstall, now sees the agent listed as enabled. Defensible — it is what "there is something of ours here" means — but it is a visible change and the deny-rule-only case is the one that reads as a lie.

**B4. `entire agent list` — `agent_group.go:69-88`**
Same widening; the `✓` marker appears against more agents, and the `"No agents installed"` hint at `:84` stops firing in leftover-artifact repos.

Only `claudecode` (`claudecode/hooks.go:470`), `pi` (`pi/hooks.go:157`) and `opencode` (`opencode/hooks.go:136`) implement `HookFreshness`, so codex/factory/cursor/gemini/copilot widening has no drift effect. See B7 for what happens to claudecode.

**B6. `entire doctor` — `doctor.go:601` `checkHookDrift`, `doctor.go:642` `checkCodexHookTrust`**
`checkCodexHookTrust` is gated on `os.Stat(.codex/hooks.json)` (`doctor.go:643-647`), **not** on `AreHooksInstalled` — unaffected, and `MissingEntireHooks`/`HookTrustGaps` in `codex/trust.go` are unchanged. `checkHookDrift` is affected via B7.

**B7. MIS-BEHAVIOUR: `checkHookDrift` goes silent on exactly the configs the widening newly reports as installed.**
`claudecode.CheckHookConfig` (`claudecode/hooks.go:476-490`) returns `HooksAbsent` when `!hasEntireHook(settings.Hooks.Stop)`. So a `.claude/settings.json` carrying only `PostToolUse` hooks, or only the deny rule, now:
- `entire status` → `Agents · Claude Code` (B3)
- `entire doctor` → prints **neither** `✓ Claude Code hook config: OK` **nor** `Claude Code hooks: OUT OF DATE`, because `checkHookDrift` treats `HooksAbsent` as "nothing to report" (`doctor.go:611-613`)
- `status --json` → agent listed, `hooks_outdated` empty

i.e. the user is told the agent is enabled and told nothing is wrong, while its `Stop` hook — the one that drives checkpointing — is missing. **Fix required in this change:** `claudecode.CheckHookConfig` must return `HooksOutdated` (not `HooksAbsent`) when detection says installed but the current spec is not met. After: it removes them and prints `Removed Codex hooks.` Same for claudecode/factory with only the deny rule or only tool-use hooks. The error path at `:1597-1602` (fail rather than uninstall blind) is unchanged.

That is the intended fix, but it is a new prompt in a case that used to be a clean no-op.

**B10. `entire enable` deselect path — `setup.go:1245` → `uninstallDeselectedAgentHooks` (`setup.go:1637-1668`)**
`installedNames` widens, so deselecting an agent with a partial config now actually removes it. Intended fix.

**B11. MIS-BEHAVIOUR: `applyAgentChanges` skips install for anything the sweep calls installed — `setup.go:552-583`, especially `:576-581`.**
`for _, name := range selectedAgentNames { if _, wasInstalled := installedSet[name]; wasInstalled { if opts.ForceHooks { reinstall } ; continue } }`. The `continue` at `:580` means a *selected* agent that the sweep reports installed gets **no** `InstallHooks` call without `--force`. Today a codex config with only `Stop` reports **not** installed → codex lands in `addedAgents` → `setupAgentHooks` runs → `InstallHooks` syncs in the missing 6 events. Not reached by: `entire enable` (`runEnableInteractive`, `setup.go:1249-1252`, calls `setupAgentHooks` for every selected agent unconditionally) or `entire agent add <name>` (`agent_group.go:118` → `setupAgentHooksNonInteractive` → `setupAgentHooks`). So the regression is scoped to the `entire agent` menu, but it is real and it is the "any enable path that skips installing when it returns true" you asked about. `InstallHooks` is idempotent for all six agents (`count==0` early return, e.g. `copilotcli/hooks.go:129`, `cursor/hooks.go:156`, `codex/hooks.go:117`), so the fix is cheap: drop the `continue` and always call `setupAgentHooks` for selected agents, using the returned count to decide whether to print "Added" vs nothing.

**B13. `copilotcli.DetectPresence` — `copilotcli/copilotcli.go:53-55`**
No change: its `AreHooksInstalled` already ORs over exactly the 8 keys uninstall touches. The only way this moves is if you count `version: 1` as owned (C4) — which would make a leftover `{"version":1}` file auto-detect Copilot in every repo that ever had it. Don't.

# C) Hazards in the mechanism

## C1. geminicli `stripNonArrayHookFields` — the real one
`geminicli/hooks.go:238-249`, called from uninstall at `:338` (return value **discarded**) and from install at `:92` as `cleanupDone`, where it is used to force a write.

It deletes any non-array value under `hooks`, i.e. the legacy `hooks.enabled: true` that old Entire versions wrote. Two facts make this the decision point:
- Gemini CLI 0.33+ **rejects** a `hooks` object with a non-array property (per the comment at `hooks.go:89-91`). So this is not cosmetic normalisation — a config left with `hooks.enabled` is a config Gemini refuses to load.
- `hooks.enabled` is unambiguously an Entire-written artifact. Nobody else put it there.

**Does conditional-on-`changed` lose something?** Yes, in exactly one case: a config with `hooks.enabled: true` and no Entire hook entries (a repo already half-cleaned). Today `UninstallHooks` strips it and writes; under a naive `changed` it would not.
**Should it count as `changed`?** Yes — and the plumbing already exists: `stripNonArrayHookFields` returns a bool, install already treats it as write-forcing, and uninstall already discards it at `:338`. OR it into `changed`. Cost, which you should accept deliberately: `AreHooksInstalled` then returns **true** for a config whose only trace is `hooks.enabled: true`, so `entire status` lists Gemini for such a repo. That is consistent with the new definition ("removal would change this config") and it is arguably right — the file is broken *by us* and we can fix it. The alternative (don't count it) leaves a config Gemini rejects on disk after a "successful" uninstall, which is worse.
**Test consequence:** `geminicli/hooks_test.go:676` keeps passing either way (its fixture has an Entire hook too). Add the no-hook-only-`enabled` case to pin the decision.

## C2. claudecode / factoryaidroid empty-container pruning
`claudecode/hooks.go:363-393` — deletes `permissions.deny` when the filtered list is empty (`:367`), deletes `permissions` when the map is empty (`:379`), deletes `hooks` when `rawHooks` is empty (`:391`). `factoryaidroid/hooks.go:357-387` is the same code.

Today, uninstalling in a repo whose `.claude/settings.json` is `{"hooks": {}, "permissions": {"deny": []}}` (no Entire artifact anywhere) rewrites it to `{}`. Under `changed`-gated writes it is left alone.
**Loses something?** Nothing a user can perceive. Empty `hooks: {}` and `deny: []` are valid, inert, and were most likely written by the user or by another tool, not by us. Claude Code does not reject them.
**Should it count as `changed`?** **No.** Counting it would make `AreHooksInstalled` return true for `{"hooks":{}}` — i.e. `entire status` would list Claude Code in any repo with an empty hooks stanza, and `entire disable --uninstall` would stop reporting "not installed" there. That is a much worse false positive than the cosmetic loss. Set `changed` only from: an Entire hook entry dropped from one of the 6/7 managed types, or the `metadataDenyRule` dropped from `permissions.deny`. Then keep the pruning as an *effect* of the write rather than a trigger for it.
**Watch out for:** the prune currently also runs when `changed` *is* true, which is what makes `TestUninstallHooks_RemovesDenyRule` (`claudecode:374`, `factoryaidroid:547`) read a permissions object that no longer exists via `readPermissions`. Keep the prune inside the pure function's write branch, not outside it.

## C3. claudecode / factoryaidroid swallowed `permissions` parse error
`claudecode/hooks.go:341-346`, `factoryaidroid/hooks.go:335-340`: `if err := json.Unmarshal(permRaw, &rawPermissions); err != nil { rawPermissions = nil }` and the cleanup is skipped silently.

Today this is a hidden uninstall bug (the deny rule survives, uninstall reports success). # Make `AreHooksInstalled` answer the same question `UninstallHooks` answers

Worktree: `/Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/cli/uninstall-ext`, branch `fix/uninstall-external-agent-hooks`.
Lands as its own commits **on that branch** (user's call).

## Context

`AreHooksInstalled` is treated everywhere as "is this agent wired up to Entire" — it gates
`entire status`, `entire agent list`, the review/investigate pickers, `entire agent remove`,
the `enable` deselect path, and now the `disable --uninstall` removal worklist. But for most
built-in agents it inspects a *narrower* set of artifacts than `UninstallHooks` removes:

| agent | probe inspects | removal touches |
| --- | --- | --- |
| claudecode | `Stop` only | 6 hook types + `permissions.deny` metadata rule |
| factoryaidroid | `Stop` only | 7 hook types + deny rule |
| codex | **all 4** `core` events, AND-wise | 7 events |
| geminicli | 11 types, OR | 11 types + `hooks.enabled` strip |
| cursor / copilotcli | matched (copilotcli hand-copies the table) | — |

So a clean "no hooks" is not evidence there is nothing to remove. `39476dc6` promoted that
probe from a display signal to a gate on whether removal runs, and the pre-existing gap turned
into a leftover-hooks bug: `.claude/settings.json` with Entire hooks under `SessionStart` +
`PreToolUse` plus the deny rule survives `entire disable --uninstall --force` while the command
reports "No agent hooks to remove" and deletes `.entire/` — leaving hooks that invoke an Entire
no longer configured there. Same leak, older, via `entire agent remove <name>` (setup.go:1596).

Patching the gate would leave the probe untrustworthy for the other six callers. The fix is to
make the probe trustworthy by construction, from one definition:

> **`AreHooksInstalled` == "removal would change this config" == at least one Entire-owned
> artifact is present.**

Monotone-safe: it is strictly wider than every current probe, so no agent that is listed today
stops being listed. "Is it *complete and current*?" is a different question and stays with
`HookFreshness`/`CheckHookConfig` and codex's `MissingEntireHooks`.

## Mechanism

Per JSON-config built-in (claudecode, cursor, geminicli, factoryaidroid, copilotcli, codex),
extract the removal into one **pure function over the file's bytes**:

```go
func removeEntireArtifacts(data []byte) (out []byte, changed bool, err error)
```

New shared helper, `cmd/entire/cli/agent/hook_file.go`, next to the existing
`DropStaleManagedHooks` / `IsManagedHookCommand` in `hook_command.go`. It owns what all six
copy today (the identical 12-line ENOENT block appears 7×):

- repo-root resolution — `paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)`, fallback `"."` (**not** `os.Getwd()`, which
  needs a `//nolint:forbidigo` here; both resolve against process cwd, so `"."` is equivalent)
- read; `os.ErrNotExist` → `(false, nil)`; any other read or parse error → error
- write via exactly `jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(x, "", "  ")` — the install writers use
  this and `testutil.AssertCommittedDogfoodConfigStable` compares bytes
- two entry points over the same removal func: one reporting `changed` (feeds
  `AreHooksInstalled`, must be **provably read-only**), one applying it and writing **only when
  `changed`** (feeds `UninstallHooks`)

### What sets `changed` — the load-bearing rule

`changed` is set **only by Entire-branded artifacts**: a hook entry whose command satisfies
`agent.IsManagedHookCommand`, the `metadataDenyRule`, geminicli's `hooks.enabled` (see below),
pi's marker. Unbranded scaffolding is pruned as an *effect* of a branded removal and never as a
*trigger*.

Getting this backwards is the trap: counting empty-container pruning would make
`{"hooks":{}}` report Claude Code installed in any repo, and counting cursor/copilotcli's
top-level `version: 1` would make a leftover file mean "Cursor installed" forever and break
every "false after uninstall" assertion.

Two deliberate exceptions to "unbranded":

- **geminicli `hooks.enabled: true`** (inside `hooks`, written by old Entire versions, stripped
  by `stripNonArrayHookFields` — `geminicli/hooks.go:238`, return value currently *discarded* at
  `:338`) **does** set `changed`. Gemini CLI 0.33+ rejects a `hooks` object with a non-array
  property, so a config left carrying it is one Gemini refuses to load — that is correctness,
  not cosmetics. Accepted cost: a repo whose only trace is `hooks.enabled` lists Gemini in
  `entire status`. Keep the strip *inside* the pure function.
- **`permissions` that fails to parse must error, not be swallowed.** `claudecode/hooks.go:341`
  and `factoryaidroid/hooks.go:335` currently do `rawPermissions = nil` on a parse failure and
  skip deny-rule cleanup. Today that is a hidden leak; under the new definition it becomes an
  advertised lie — `"permissions": "oops"` + a live deny rule would move from "could not check →
  uninstall warns and exits non-zero" to "cleanly reported nothing to remove", the exact failure
  this branch exists to prevent.

Keep the transforms on the raw-map representation (`map[string]json.RawMessage`), not typed
structs — a large set of round-trip tests pins that unknown hook types and foreign keys survive
(`claudecode:793`, `factoryaidroid:615`, `geminicli:283`, `cursor:428`, `copilotcli:322`,
`codex:262`). Note also that geminicli's uninstall must **not** route through
`writeGeminiSettingsFile` (`geminicli/hooks.go:252`), which injects `hooksConfig`.

`codex`: drop the `core` field (`codex/hooks.go:33-64`) and its three comments — detection
becomes OR-over-`managedHooks`. Codex is already the template here: install, uninstall and
detect all iterate one table. Its `rawHooks == nil → return nil` early-out (`:186`) is the
existing precedent for `changed=false`. Rewrite the contract prose in `codex/AGENT.md:259`.

pi, opencode (whole generated file + marker) and vogon (no-op) keep their current shape — their
detect already coincides with removal. External plugin agents are unchanged: the protocol owns
both answers.

## Also in scope (leftover artifacts — user's call)

Same rule throughout: prune only as an effect of a branded removal, so detection stays honest.

- **cursor / copilotcli `version: 1`**: after removal, if the only remaining top-level key is
  `version`, delete the file (`.cursor/hooks.json`, `.github/hooks/entire.json`). Must not fire
  when the user has other keys — `cursor/hooks_test.go:499` and `copilotcli:322` pin that
  `cursorSettings` / `copilotSettings` / `hooks.onNotification` survive.
- **geminicli `hooksConfig.enabled: true`** (top-level, `hooks.go:96`): remove the key, and
  `hooksConfig` when it is then empty, **only when** a branded removal happened *and* the
  resulting `hooks` is empty. Never counts toward `changed` — counting it would pin
  `AreHooksInstalled` true forever after uninstall.
- **pi's `os.RemoveAll(filepath.Dir(path))`** (`pi/hooks.go:108`): narrow to removing the
  marker-carrying file, then remove the directory only if it is then empty. Install already
  refuses to overwrite foreign files; uninstall should match.

## Two consequences that must be fixed in the same change

**1. `claudecode.CheckHookConfig` goes silent on exactly the configs detection newly reports as
installed** (`claudecode/hooks.go:476`). It returns `HooksAbsent` when
`!hasEntireHook(settings.Hooks.Stop)`, and `doctor.go:611` treats `HooksAbsent` as nothing to
report. So a config with only `PostToolUse` hooks or only the deny rule would say: `status` →
"Claude Code" listed; `doctor` → neither OK nor OUT OF DATE; `status --json` → `hooks_outdated`
empty — while the `Stop` hook that drives checkpointing is missing. Gate its absent-branch on
the same "any owned artifact" predicate as the new probe, then let the existing positive-spec
checks (`:483-487`) decide current-vs-outdated. (factoryaidroid has no `CheckHookConfig` at all;
note it, don't add one here.)

**2. `applyAgentChanges` skips install for anything the sweep calls installed**
(`setup.go:552-583`, the `continue` at `:580`). Reached by `entire agent` (bare) →
`runManageAgents`. Today a codex config with only `Stop` reports not-installed, so codex is
treated as newly added and `InstallHooks` repairs it. After the widening it reports installed
and is skipped without `--force`, so **a partial install is never repaired**. `InstallHooks` is
idempotent for all six agents (`count == 0` early return), so drop the `continue`, always call
`setupAgentHooks` for selected agents, and use the returned count to decide what to print.
`entire enable` and `entire agent add` already call it unconditionally.

## Accepted, reported, not fixed here

- `entire investigate/review --agent <name>` (`investigate/cmd.go:833` `verifyAgentsLaunchable`)
  currently hard-errors on a partial config and will now launch a degraded run instead. These
  pickers are the one consumer where "installed" genuinely meant "fully wired". With fix #1
  above, `status` and `doctor` report the drift; moving the pickers onto `HookFreshness` is a
  follow-up.
- Detection now pays a full parse+transform per agent per sweep, and `getAgentHookState` runs on
  every command (`root.go:83`, telemetry). Six raw-map round-trips is microseconds; noted, not
  redesigned. There is a benchmark on the enable hot path (`bench_enable_test.go`) but not the sweep.
- Telemetry agent attribution (`root.go:83`) widens, so "repos with agent X enabled" steps up
  discontinuously at this release. Worth telling whoever reads that dashboard.
- pi stays the counterexample to the invariant, so write the contract comment on
  `agent.HookSupport` as covering the JSON-config built-ins rather than asserting it universally.

## Tests (TDD — failing first)

Repo-level regression, the peer's exact repro, in `cmd/entire/cli/setup_test.go`: write
`.claude/settings.json` carrying Entire hooks under `SessionStart` + `PreToolUse` plus the deny
rule and **no `Stop`**, run `runUninstall(ctx, &stdout, &stderr, true)`, assert the file carries
no `entire hooks ` command and no `Read(./.entire/metadata/**)` rule, and that stdout reports
hooks removed rather than "No agent hooks to remove". Same shape for `entire agent remove`.

Per-agent detect tests (each agent's `hooks_test.go`), one per behaviour with a doc comment
stating the invariant, matching the file's conventions:

- claudecode: `SessionStart` only → installed; deny rule only → installed
- factoryaidroid: `PreToolUse` only → installed
- codex: `Stop` only → installed (**inverts** `TestAreHooksInstalled_PartialHooks`,
  `codex/hooks_test.go:318`, which today asserts `false` — the only test in the tree asserting
  false for a config containing an Entire artifact. Invert it and add a companion assertion that
  `MissingEntireHooks` still reports the gap, so the installed/freshness split stays pinned)
- geminicli: `hooks.enabled: true` with no Entire hook → installed, and uninstall strips it
- claudecode/factoryaidroid: unparseable `permissions` + live deny rule → **error**, and
  `getAgentHookState` classifies it `unchecked`
- negative guards for the `changed` rule: `{"hooks":{}}` → not installed;
  `{"version":1}` alone → not installed

Shape-agnostic conformance loop in `cmd/entire/cli/setup_test.go` (that package has every
built-in registered): for each built-in `HookSupport` agent except `agent.TestOnly` ones, in a
fresh `setupTestRepo(t)` — `InstallHooks` → detect true → `UninstallHooks` → detect false and no
`entire hooks ` substring left in the config → second `UninstallHooks` is a no-op. Non-parallel,
with the one-line reason comment the file uses.

Must keep passing (they are the shared helper's contract, don't regress them):
`setup_test.go:1473` `TestRunUninstall_HalfUninstallRecoversOnRerun` (chmod 0o000 → the read
error must surface as an error, not `false`); every per-agent
`TestUninstallHooks_Unreadable*Errors`; `copilotcli/hooks_test.go:537`, whose assertion requires
the parse error string to keep containing `"failed to parse"`; the three
`AssertCommittedDogfoodConfigStable` callers (byte-exact install output);
`geminicli/hooks_test.go:676` `TestUninstallHooks_RemovesLegacyEnabledField`.

Stale comments to correct while nearby: `setup_test.go:2951` and `:2968` both describe the old
probe rule; `agent/agent.go:124-133` (the `AreHooksInstalled` contract — state the new
definition *and* that it does not mean "fully installed") and `:151-159` (`HookFreshness`, which
now also covers the JSON-config agents).

## Files

- new: `cmd/entire/cli/agent/hook_file.go` (shared read/plan/apply helper)
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/agent.go` — the contract lives here (`:124-133`, `:151-159`)
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/{claudecode,cursor,geminicli,factoryaidroid,copilotcli,codex}/hooks.go`
  — pure `removeEntireArtifacts`, both entry points derived from it; plus
  `claudecode/hooks.go:470` `CheckHookConfig`, `codex/hooks.go:33-64` `core` removal,
  `geminicli/hooks.go:238/338` strip
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/pi/hooks.go:108` — narrow the `RemoveAll`
- `cmd/entire/cli/setup.go:552-583` — `applyAgentChanges` install skip
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/AGENT.md:259` — the `core` contract prose
- tests as above

The gate in `uninstallAgentHooks` (`setup.go:2703`) and
`TestRunUninstall_BuiltinNotDetectedIsLeftAlone` (`setup_test.go:1850`) need **no change**: once
detect==remove by construction, "the sweep said none" *is* proof removal is a no-op, so acting
on exactly the sweep's answer is correct rather than merely tolerated. This also answers the open
design question — `UninstallHooks` does not need to grow a "changed anything" return (which would
mean changing the external-plugin protocol), because the report keyed on a trustworthy sweep is
already accurate.

## Verification

```
mise run fmt && mise run lint        # single sequence; re-lint if fmt rewrote anything
mise run test:ci
```

Then the manual repro, in a throwaway repo: `.claude/settings.json` with Entire `SessionStart` +
`PreToolUse` hooks and the deny rule but no `Stop` → `entire disable --uninstall --force` →
assert none of the three artifacts remain and the output names Claude Code. Repeat with a
`.codex/hooks.json` carrying only `SubagentStop`, and with `entire agent remove claude-code`
instead of the uninstall. Finally `entire status` and `entire doctor` in a partial-config repo:
the agent must be listed *and* reported out of date, not listed and silent.

Note: `mise run lint` can fail locally on a stale golangci-lint v1 shadowing v2.11.3 — run the
mise-installed binary directly if that happens.

Plan agreed and approved by the user. Full plan file: /Users/gtrrz-victor/.claude/plans/cross-session-message-from-uds-tmp-cc-s-sorted-ritchie.md — read it and implement it in your worktree. Two user decisions constrain it: (a) it lands as its own commits ON fix/uninstall-external-agent-hooks, not a stacked PR; (b) the known install/uninstall leftovers are in scope too.

Headline: do NOT fix the gate. The user rejected that direction outright — "I need both methods... that would make everything use that method prone to failures, like entire enable/entire status/entire doctor. arehooksinstalled should be trustable. Fix it, in a way we don't duplicate that logic for uninstall and check if it is installed for all our built in agents."

So the fix is one definition, applied to every JSON-config built-in:

  AreHooksInstalled == "removal would change this config" == at least one Entire-owned artifact is present.

Mechanism: per agent, extract removal into a pure `removeEntireArtifacts(data []byte) (out []byte, changed bool, err error)`; new shared helper `cmd/entire/cli/agent/hook_file.go` owns repo-root resolution, the ENOENT-vs-error split (currently copy-pasted 7×), and write-only-when-changed, with two entry points over that one function — a read-only one feeding AreHooksInstalled, an applying one feeding UninstallHooks. codex is already the template (managedHooks); its `core` field goes away, and freshness stays with MissingEntireHooks / CheckHookConfig. Widening is monotone, so nothing listed today stops being listed.

Your open design question resolves to "no interface change": once detect==remove by construction, the sweep's answer IS proof removal is a no-op, so `uninstallAgentHooks` acting on exactly the sweep is correct rather than merely tolerated, and UninstallHooks does not need a "changed anything" return (which would have meant changing the external-plugin protocol). TestRunUninstall_BuiltinNotDetectedIsLeftAlone needs no inversion — it stays valid as written.

The load-bearing rule, and the trap: `changed` is set ONLY by Entire-branded artifacts (a command satisfying IsManagedHookCommand, the metadataDenyRule, geminicli's `hooks.enabled`, pi's marker). Unbranded scaffolding is pruned as an EFFECT of a branded removal, never as a trigger. Invert that and `{"hooks":{}}` reports Claude Code installed in every repo, and a leftover `{"version":1}` means Cursor forever.

Three things the ripple analysis turned up that you must handle in the same change, all with file:line in the plan:
1. claudecode.CheckHookConfig gates its absent-branch on `Stop` too, so the newly-detected partial configs get listed by status and reported as nothing-wrong by doctor — while the Stop hook that drives checkpointing is missing.
2. applyAgentChanges (setup.go:580) skips InstallHooks for anything the sweep calls installed, so after the widening a partial install is never repaired via the `entire agent` menu.
3. claudecode/factoryaidroid swallow an unparseable `permissions` (`rawPermissions = nil`). Today that's a hidden leak; under the new definition it becomes an advertised lie — it must error so getAgentHookState classifies it `unchecked`.

Tests are TDD-first and enumerated in the plan, including the one test in the tree that legitimately inverts (codex/hooks_test.go:318, which asserts false for a config containing an Entire hook) and the set that must keep passing because they ARE the shared helper's contract. Ping me when it's implemented and I'll review the diff.

One decision needs you. The codex status test asserts:

> ignored worktree-local hooks must not report Codex installed

In a linked worktree Codex reads its hooks from elsewhere, so a worktree-local `.codex/hooks.json` never fires. But that guarantee was **never actually implemented** — main's detection had no worktree-awareness at all; the test passed only because its fixture is a single `Stop` hook, which main's "all core events" gate rejected anyway. A *complete* install in a linked worktree reports Codex installed on main today. There is already a dedicated diagnostic for this case (`codex_hooks: inactive_in_worktree`), and it keys on the same "any Entire hook present" predicate my change uses.

Your "keep it unlisted" answer isn't implementable — I gave you an incomplete picture, so let me correct it. Three tests constrain codex in a linked worktree:

| fixture | required outcome | source |
|---|---|---|
| **complete** worktree-local config | **must** be listed installed | `doctor_test.go:899` |
| **complete** worktree-local config | **must** be removed on deselect | `..._CodexLinkedWorktreeOwnership` |
| **partial** (Stop-only) config | must **not** be listed | `..._InactiveDiscovery` |

The only rule satisfying all three is a completeness gate — main's "all core events" AND — which is exactly the untrustworthy probe we're removing. So codex can't both stand down in linked worktrees and have a derived probe. With detection derived (worktree file, any Entire hook), the entire suite passes except that one `Agents` assertion.

options.label: Derived; update that assertion (Recommended)
options.description: Codex detection = any Entire hook in the file Entire writes here — same predicate as removal, no exceptions. A partial linked-worktree config now lists Codex, consistent with how a complete one already behaves, and `codex_hooks: NOT ACTIVE IN THIS WORKTREE` still tells the user those hooks don't fire. I change the one `Agents` assertion in the status test and leave its other three assertions (which are its real subject) untouched.

options.label: Keep a completeness gate for codex only

Cost: codex keeps the exact narrow-probe bug for non-core hooks — `entire agent remove codex` on a SubagentStop-only config still says "not installed" and leaves it. Contradicts the point of the change.

# Ship Changes

Commit current changes, push to remote, and update the PR.

## Step 1: Analyze changes

1. Run `git diff --stat` and `git diff` to understand what changed
2. Run `git status` to see untracked files
3. Run `git log --oneline -3` to match the repo's commit message style

## Step 2: Commit

1. Stage only the relevant changed/untracked files by name (never `git add -A` or `git add .`)
2. Write a concise commit message that focuses on the "why" not the "what"
   - If `as draft PR` is provided, use it as the commit message
   - Otherwise, draft one from the diff
3. Commit. If hooks fail, diagnose and fix — do NOT use `--no-verify`

## Step 3: Push

1. Check if the branch tracks a remote: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{u}`
2. If not tracking, push with `-u origin <branch>`
3. If tracking, just `git push`
4. If push is rejected (remote has new commits), pull with rebase first then push

## Step 4: Update PR

1. Find the open PR for the current branch: `gh pr view --json number,body,title`
2. If no PR exists, skip this step and inform the user
3. Compare the current PR body against the new changes:
   - If the changes are within the existing PR scope, update the description to reflect the current state
   - If the changes are additive or a follow-up, add a PR comment summarizing what was just pushed instead
4. When updating the PR body, preserve the overall structure but refresh the summary bullets and test plan
5. When adding a comment, keep it concise — bullet points of what changed and why
6. **Before making any PR update (description edit or comment), show the user the exact text you plan to post and ask for their approval. Do NOT post until they confirm.**

## Rules

- Never commit files that look like secrets (.env, credentials, tokens)
- Never force push
- Always show the user what was committed and the PR URL when done

both answers from it, so detection cannot be narrower than removal by
construction: agent.HookArtifactsInstalled reports whether removal would change
anything, agent.RemoveHookArtifacts performs it and now writes only when it does.

content.text:
Answering directly: **no, it doesn't.** `claudeSettingsPath` currently feeds only detection and removal — `InstallHooks` at line 70 still builds its own. And there's a third one I missed entirely: `loadClaudeSettings` at line 438 is a character-for-character duplicate of the helper.

Across all five agents:

| site | resolution | vs `HookConfigPath` |
|---|---|---|
| claudecode `loadClaudeSettings:438` | `WorktreeRoot`, `"."` fallback | **identical** — a straight miss |
| cursor:58, copilotcli:44 (install) | `WorktreeRoot`, `"."` fallback | **identical** |
| claudecode:70, geminicli:55, factoryaidroid:56 (install) | `WorktreeRoot`, `os.Getwd()` fallback | same file in practice; differs only if `Getwd` fails, and carries a `//nolint:forbidigo` |

That also makes the doc comment I wrote on `HookConfigPath` — "Install, detection and removal have to agree on this path, so they share one resolution of it" — false as it stands. Fixing the code rather than the comment:

	data, err := os.ReadFile(settingsPath) //nolint:gosec // path is constructed from repo root + fixed path''')
